# Sentinel's Security Journal

## 2026-10-21 - Restrict Mermaid Security Level to Strict to Prevent Stored/DOM XSS
**Vulnerability:** Mermaid was initialized with `securityLevel: 'loose'` in `app/src/lib/mermaid.ts`. The rendered SVG strings generated by Mermaid diagrams are directly inserted into the DOM via `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` in `DiagramViewer` and `MarkdownDiagram`. Under `loose` mode, Mermaid allows raw HTML tags, embedded scripts, and javascript event handlers within diagram DSL code, enabling stored or DOM-based cross-site scripting (XSS) when untrusted or LLM-generated paper diagram definitions are viewed.
**Learning:** Even though diagrams are generated through LLM extraction pipelines, model outputs or paper extractions cannot be inherently trusted as safe from script injection. Furthermore, any client-rendered SVG component using `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` must either strictly sanitize the SVG or configure the underlying rendering engine in its most secure mode.
**Prevention:** Always configure `mermaid.initialize` with `securityLevel: 'strict'` to sanitize HTML tags and forbid executable script callbacks/tags inside diagram syntax.
